doc.title: Elvin Jones — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Aftermath: returning to Japan and Kenny Clarke replacing him
summary: The tour continued, Elvin lost drums, and Keiko took him back to Japan yearly to clear his name.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: (Laughs) Okay well that fills in a lot of gaps for ’67.
We had the chief of the USSIS and his wife as our guests and the ambassador wrote a beautiful introduction of our program and it came out very well.
That’s the only way I take him to Japan. From that moment every year I took him to clear up his name. From next year we have hard time cause we have to stay at hotel in airport.
Yes. I don’t mind and I explain to Elvin everything and 5 to 6 years later he is the only one who was deported to Japan and come back. He was the only one left free.
What happened to Tony? Was he let free because…Was he let free because he put him in?
So he went back with the rest of the tour, and you’re the only one who had to stay behind?

Well he didn’t go back with the tour, he was deported, cause the rest of the tour was going on. You know, Kenny Clarke had to take his place, to fill in. And he stayed about three days and he said, “Let me get out of here!” (Laughs)
